scope.q: What specific metrics define 'too far' and what is the current baseline or target for picker travel distance per order or per shift?
scope.why: Understanding the precise definition of the problem and desired improvement quantifies success and informs data analysis priorities.

scope.q: What are the physical constraints of the warehouse layout (e.g., shelving types, aisle widths, one-way paths, restricted zones) and how frequently does this layout change?
scope.why: The physical environment heavily dictates potential optimization strategies and the feasibility of implementing changes.

scope.q: Are there existing picking strategies (e.g., batch picking, zone picking, pick-to-light) in place, and what is the current WMS's capability to integrate with or enforce new routing algorithms?
scope.why: Knowing current operational modes and WMS flexibility determines the scope of potential solutions and integration complexity.

decomposition.title: WMS Data Ingestion & Validation
decomposition.why: This foundational step ensures we have reliable and complete data from the WMS to analyze picker movements.

decomposition.title: Picker Path Reconstruction & Visualization
decomposition.why: Reconstructing and visualizing picker paths is essential to understand current inefficiencies and identify specific problem areas.

decomposition.title: Warehouse Layout & Item Location Modeling
decomposition.why: A precise model of the warehouse and item locations is crucial for accurate path calculations and optimization simulations.

decomposition.title: Path Optimization Algorithm Development
decomposition.why: Developing an algorithm to suggest more efficient picking paths is the core problem-solving component.

decomposition.title: Simulation & Impact Analysis
decomposition.why: Simulating optimized paths against historical data allows us to quantify potential savings before operational changes.

sprint.title: WMS Data Connector & Schema Definition
sprint.deliv: Working script ingesting sample WMS pick data into a raw data store, with schema defined.

sprint.title: Basic Path Reconstruction & Visualization
sprint.deliv: A script that plots a single picker's historical path on a simplified grid representation of the warehouse.

sprint.title: Warehouse Layout Data Model & Ingestion
sprint.deliv: Database with initial warehouse layout (aisles, shelves) and item locations, populated from provided data.

sprint.title: First-Pass Path Optimization Algorithm
sprint.deliv: An algorithm that takes a list of pick locations and returns a shortest path, tested against a few manual examples.

sprint.title: Simulation Framework & Baseline Metrics
sprint.deliv: A framework that can run the optimization algorithm on historical data and calculate total distance saved.

sprint.title: Interactive Analytics Dashboard (MVP)
sprint.deliv: Web dashboard displaying current picker travel distances, optimized distances, and a comparison for selected historical orders.

risks.risk: WMS data lacks precise location timestamps or granular item pick events, making accurate path reconstruction difficult.
risks.mitigation: Conduct an early deep dive into WMS data logs with a WMS expert to confirm data availability and granularity. If insufficient, explore alternative data sources like scanner logs or picker GPS/RFID data.

risks.risk: Warehouse layout data (e.g., precise coordinates of shelves, aisles, and item bins) is incomplete, outdated, or unavailable.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize obtaining accurate layout CAD files or conducting a physical survey. Develop a user interface for manual layout adjustments and validation by warehouse staff.

risks.risk: Optimized paths might be theoretically efficient but impractical due to real-world constraints not captured in the model (e.g., congestion, temporary obstructions, picker preferences).
risks.mitigation: Incorporate a feedback loop from warehouse operations. Start with simulation, then pilot with a small group of pickers, gathering qualitative and quantitative feedback to refine the algorithm and model.

risks.risk: The WMS integration for pushing optimized routes back into operational systems is complex or requires significant custom development.
risks.mitigation: Early engagement with WMS vendor or internal WMS team to understand API capabilities and limitations. Design the recommendation API to be modular, allowing for manual input or phased integration.
